concept.name: Fixed-range volume profile
concept.definition: A volume profile computed over a user-selected, fixed span of the chart — the analyst manually anchors the start and end points, and the histogram shows how volume distributed across price levels within exactly that range. It isolates the volume structure of a chosen move, range, or event window.
concept.intuition: Instead of accepting session boundaries, you draw a box around the exact move you care about and ask: where inside this move did volume actually concentrate?
concept.mechanics: The user sets two anchor points; tick or lower-timeframe volume between them is binned by price into a horizontal histogram displaying the range's POC, value area (VAH/VAL), and high/low-volume nodes; the profile stays fixed regardless of scrolling.
concept.failure_modes: Anchor placement is entirely discretionary, so levels can be unconsciously curve-fit to support a thesis; changing anchors even slightly can move the POC and value area.
concept.misconceptions: FRVP levels are not more objective than session levels because they are 'custom' — they inherit the analyst's framing choice, and platform documentation explicitly warns against expecting tick-precise bounces off such POCs.
concept.example: A trader anchors a profile from a swing low at 4,400 to the rally high at 4,520; the FRVP shows an HVN at 4,470–4,485, which is then watched as potential support on the pullback.
